articles.summary: Developer handbook for the kernel and bundled plugins. APIs, openings, storage, and how each surface actually works.

blocks.title: Developers and agents
blocks.text: Write a plugin, extend checkout, or teach an IA the shop without reading the whole repo. This is not operator help. Disable the Documentation plugin and the menu disappears; the shop keeps running.

blocks.title: No identity cards

articles.title: How the shop is built
articles.summary: Kernel versus plugin versus complement, and what must never leave core.

items.title: Kernel
items.text: Always on: catalogue, cart, checkout, orders, accounts, the admin shell, plugin host, SEO engine, payment-method, courier, and email shells.

items.title: Plugin
items.text: A folder with package.json (tuucho block) and back/register.ts. Enable loads it. Disable unloads it. Tables stay until uninstall. For a public page, enable is also the shop menu entry.

items.title: Complement
items.text: dependsOn another plugin id. If a required parent is off, isPluginEffectivelyEnabled is false. The runtime does not auto-enable dependencies.

blocks.title: Do not extract these
blocks.text: Collection, users, orders, stock, roles, vocabulary, shop axes, checkout, and the plugin host stay in core. Contact is tuucho-contact. Cursor plugin skills still refuse to extract catalogue or checkout.

items.description: Shop name, product axes, vocabulary, Preferences, Roles, users, impersonation.
Orders, stock, collection. Payment-method and courier shells are kernel lists that plugins register into.
SMTP, mail_jobs, sendMail / sendTemplatedMail. Plugins call api.sendMail. They do not own SMTP. Who receives spy/ops copies is tuucho-mail-spy.
My profile, sign-in methods, and notifications are kernel screens. Plugins add rows through openings.

articles.title: Config files
articles.summary: Shop-root tuucho-config JSON for the kernel, plus plugin JSON under tuucho-config/plugins/<id>/. Files seed once; the DB stays the runtime source of truth.

blocks.title: Kernel JSON does not name plugin keys
blocks.text: tuucho-config/config.json is http, paths, database, session, smtp shell, security, logs. Plugin credentials live on that plugin settingsSchema. Required private kernel paths: database.url, jwt.secret, pii.encryptionKey, pii.lookupPepper, ops.token.

Merge matches boot: common public, env public, common private-or-example, env private-or-example. Public JSON is committed. Private JSON is gitignored. Apply / Tuucho updates never write tuucho-config/.

blocks.text: plugins.settings (plaintext) and plugins.secrets (sealed AES-256-GCM) are the live values. Files are an operator input/export surface. Boot never overwrites Admin. First launch loads files once when secrets are empty and public keys are missing, blank, or still defaultSettings.

blocks.title: Separate from Configure save
blocks.text: Holding preferences does not grant import or export. Holding import does not grant export. super-admin has the catalogue; user (customer) has none. Staff roles are off until granted on Roles.

Admin → Plugins (list) has Update all, Import all, and Export all next to Scan. Same two permission codes. Plugins without settingsSchema never participate. Bulk never enables or disables a plugin. Writes go to the DB only, not back onto tuucho-config/.

items.description: Disk JSON → DB for every enabled schema plugin that has files. Disabled plugins are skipped. Disk files stay flat (no envelope).

One zip or tgz. Named plugin ids are written even if disabled, and are not enabled. Unnamed disabled plugins stay untouched. Unknown ids are skipped. Not all-or-nothing across the shop; each plugin is one transaction.

blocks.text: Archive layout: <plugin-id>/config.json and <plugin-id>/config.private.json. An optional shared root folder is stripped. Filename still config.json / config.private.json. Path id must match envelope pluginId.

blocks.caption: Envelope format 1 (archive members and downloads only; placeholders)

blocks.title: Unsafe apply is blocked
blocks.text: No DB write for that plugin when: id not installed, no settingsSchema, envelope format is not 1, shop core misses compat.core, installed plugin version misses compat.plugin, path id ≠ envelope id, layer ≠ filename, or a public payload contains secret keys. HTTP for a single blocked per-plugin import: 409 plugin_config_incompatible or 400 invalid_request. Zip-slip / not an archive: 400 invalid_archive and zero writes. Never log secret values.

articles.title: Plugin register API
articles.summary: The object back/register.ts receives: filters, actions, services, shells, HTTP mounts, cache, mail.

blocks.title: From @tuucho/plugin-sdk
blocks.text: export const register: PluginRegisterFn = async (api) => { ... }. There is no db, settings, or logger on api. Query through your own application helpers. Kernel wraps client.query in plugin migrations and rejects SQL that mutates tables you do not own.

items.description: This package id and the parsed leaf package.json tuucho block plus npm version/description/repository.

Fire-and-forget. Kernel actions include plugin.enabled.changed and cron.process-shipment-tracking.
Publish a public object under a plugin id. Callers use peekPluginService or getPluginService from the SDK, not from api.
Payment plugins only. Kernel checkout lists methods while the plugin is on.
Shipping plugins only. courierCodes on the method and on the manifest.
scope: admin, account, public, operation. Typed scope plugin is not wired in the kernel today.
Per-plugin namespace: get, set, del, flush. set({ ttl, sensitivity: 'public' | 'private' }). Public keys cannot look like secrets.
Named mail bodies and locale overlays for email.
Kernel email shell. Plugins never own SMTP. Unbound host throws mail_shell_unbound.

blocks.text: The kernel owns the method lists. A payment plugin calls registerPaymentGateway({ id, methods, capabilities, Stripe-like ops }). articles.title: Create with Cursor
articles.summary: Point an agent at the router skill. It loads one specialized child skill and does not edit the kernel.

items: Use .cursor/skills/tuucho-create-plugin/SKILL.md.
It picks page, admin, slot, opening, schema, locale, payment, shipping, permission, SEO, UI, or spy channel, then reads exactly one child SKILL.md.
If the opening you need does not exist, it stops and tells you.

blocks.title: Stay in core
blocks.text: The skill will not move collection, contact, users, orders, stock, roles, vocabulary, or shop axes into a plugin.

articles.title: Publishing a plugin for updates
articles.summary: How a third party must publish so Admin, Plugins, Check for updates can walk git tags.

blocks.title: Official Tuucho is one repo
blocks.text: Kernel and every tuucho-* plugin update only from https://github.com/by-tezov/tuucho-ecom tags (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, never a v prefix). There is no per-plugin GitHub for Tuucho. plugins/user/ is never overwritten by a Tuucho Apply. Plugins Core and Check current are the live root package.json version. Latest is the newest official tag. Local ahead of that tag has no Apply. shop-release.json is last-applied Apply state, not displayed current.

A user plugin may set npm repository on package.json to an HTTPS GitHub repo root. Check uses that origin for that plugin id only. Missing repository means zip-only. Complements are separate packages.

rows: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Order is semver. No v prefix. No master HEAD.
package.json version equals the tag (1.2.0 means 1.2.0).
Repo root is the package: package.json with a tuucho block and back/register.ts at the zipball root.
[a-z0-9-]+ and must not start with tuucho-.
Additive back/migrations. Never rewrite an applied up. Tables plugin_<id>_... only.
Every tag between the shop version and latest must be bootable. The shop walks 2 then 3 then 4 then 5.

blocks.caption: plugin-release.json on every tag (required for updates)
blocks.code:
{
  "id": "gift-wrap",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "tag": "1.2.0",
  "releaseId": 4,
  "migrations": ["001_tables.js"],
  "changelog": "Adds gift-wrap SKUs."
}

blocks.text: releaseId strictly increases. Set npm repository on package.json to the repo root URL.

items: missing package.json tuucho block or back/register.ts

missing description on a non-locale plugin
engines.core or dependsOn mismatch
git tag 1.2.0 with package.json version 1.1.0, or a v-prefixed tag
releaseId hole or decrease
non-GitHub or non-HTTPS repository
private repo (v1 sends no GitHub token)
id change across tags

blocks.title: Apply
blocks.text: Admin, Plugins: Check for updates, then Apply. A third-party Apply replaces that folder only, after a snapshot. Failure restores the snapshot. Updates never uninstall.

articles.title: Installing and applying shop updates
articles.summary: Clone a tag, then Check and Apply from Admin, Plugins. What is never touched, how jumps walk tags, and how rollback works.

items: git clone --branch 0.0.2 --depth 1 https://github.com/by-tezov/tuucho-ecom.git
npm run setup:cli (or npm run setup on :8787)
npm run dev. Shop on 5174. Setup writes shop-release.json next to installed.lock.

blocks.text: You do not git-pull later. Check for updates reads git tags only, never untagged master. Plugins Core and Check current are this product's live root package.json. Latest is the newest official tag. A checkout newer than that tag is ahead of the published tag (no Apply). Matching versions: nothing to update. Older local: walk every tag. Last applied official tag is shop-release.json.

items: Admin, Plugins: Check for updates.
Read the tag path (0.0.2 to 0.0.3 to 0.0.4). Scope All, Kernel, or Tuucho plugins. One plugin Apply is on that row.
Confirm. Apply snapshots, then walks every tag. The overlay log stays until you close it.

blocks.title: No skipping
blocks.text: A shop on tag 1 with latest 5 applies 2 then 3 then 4 then 5. Latest-only would skip migrations that later tags deleted.

blocks.title: Local edits under plugins/tuucho
blocks.text: Check hashes the bundled tree. If it disagrees with the recorded tag, Apply is refused until you copy those edits out (or into a plugins/user plugin). There is no force in v1.

Apply snapshots the database and the scoped files first. Any thrown step restores that snapshot and stops. A later go-back to an older tag is restore-from-backup, not walking down. Kernel Apply may ask you to restart the API process.

blocks.title: GitHub egress
blocks.text: The shop server must reach github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, and codeload.github.com over HTTPS. Official origin is public; v1 sends no token. Private third-party repos fail Check. Zip upload remains for first install and for publishers without repository.

articles.title: Storage and uninstall
articles.summary: Plugin-owned tables, disable versus uninstall, and how to read kernel data.

blocks.title: No ALTER of kernel tables
blocks.text: Extra data lives in plugin_<id with underscores>_… from back/migrations/*.js with up(client) and down(client). Foreign keys may point at users, orders, or products. The host wraps client.query and rejects SQL that mutates any other table.

rows: Unloads code. Tables, settings, and schema_version stay.
POST /admin/plugins/:id/uninstall with confirm true: down, drop leftover plugin tables, delete the row.
Admin → Plugins shows Folder missing. Uninstall to drop tables, or restore the folder.

blocks.text: Kernel contact, orders, and stock tables are not plugin tables. Read them through kernel HTTP or openings. Do not ALTER unconnected_contacts or orders from a plugin migration.

articles.title: Courier on the cart
articles.summary: How a shipping plugin registers methods and packet prices.

items: kind shipping, provides ShippingMethod, courierCodes lists the rows you own.
registerShippingMethod({ id, courierCodes, ensureCouriers }). Checkout keeps a courier only while its plugin is on.
Packet prices are edited on the kernel Couriers JSON page (PUT /admin/courier-catalog/couriers/:code). Disable the plugin and those couriers leave the cart.

articles.title: Loyalty on checkout
articles.summary: How commerce-loyalty injects extraLines and stores a snapshot on the order.

items.title: Off
items.text: Credit is zero. Wallet UI is hidden.

items.title: On
items.text: checkout.quote priority 30 adds extraLines and plugins[tuucho-commerce-loyalty]. Confirm consumes a hold. Snapshot copies the bag.

items.title: Later off
items.text: Past orders keep the snapshot. New UI is hidden. Checkout pricing is server-authoritative.

blocks.text: Service id is tuucho-commerce-loyalty (peekPluginService). HTTP mounts: admin /loyalty, account /loyalty, operation /loyalty. Permission loyalty. Dashboard card uses slot.admin.dashboard and ui.AdminStatCard (the stats grid owns width).

articles.title: A staff permission
articles.summary: From manifest to Roles to requirePermission.

items: permissions[] on the manifest.
Admin → Roles can grant it while the plugin is on.
requirePermission plus requirePluginEnabled on the router. Nav: access and pluginId. Super-admin sees the section without a stored grant.

articles.title: Register a spy channel
articles.summary: Declare who should be configurable for an ops e-mail. tuucho-mail-spy owns recipients; the kernel still sends SMTP.

items: addFilter mail.spy.channels with appendSpyChannel: id, pluginId, title, description, filters (role, email, kind).
Send with spyTo('your_id') then sendMail. Empty To skips.
Operators pick roles and/or staff emails on Admin → Spy e-mails. Customers never receive. One address, one copy.
